neutral_facts.value: The accused, who was married to the deceased, was alleged to have caused her death by burning. The prosecution claimed that the deceased suffered serious burn injuries in the kitchen around 7:00 a.m. on February 6, 1990, and later died from those injuries. The deceased made a dying declaration to a police officer on February 9, 1990, stating that she had quarreled with her husband over household chores and the feeding of children, then poured kerosene on herself and set herself on fire. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 498-A and 306 of the IPC and sentenced him to one year and four years respectively. The High Court enhanced the sentence under Section 306 from four to six years. The Supreme Court quashed the High Court's enhanced sentence and confirmed the trial court's judgment.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Appellant's appeal dismissed; High Court: State's appeal allowed, sentence enhanced; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, High Court's sentence quashed, Trial Court's judgment confirmed

quotes.text: The appeal filed by the appellant was dismissed. The appeal filed by the State was allowed and the sentence awarded by the Trial Court under Section 306 IPC was enhanced from four to six years. It is in this situation that the matter is before us.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the deceased made a dying declaration stating she had a quarrel with her husband over household chores and feeding of children, and then poured kerosene on herself and burnt herself.

quotes.text: The prosecution case that at about 8.30 a.m. on the 9th February 1990 she made a dying declaration to PW.10 - a Police Head Constable, in which she stated that she had a quarrel with her husband over the house-hold chores and over the feeding of the children and she had thereafter poured kerosene on herself and then burnt herself.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the High Court was not justified in enhancing the sentence on account of the accused's quarrelsome nature, as the incident was a spontaneous family quarrel and the trial court had already found no misbehaviour over a period of time.

quotes.text: The learned counsel for the appellant has made only one argument before us. He has submitted that the High Court had observed that the appellant appeared to be of a quarrelsome and aggressive nature and as evidence of his behaviour had placed reliance on two letters which required that a heavy sentence should be imposed.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that appellate courts should rarely interfere with the quantum of sentence and only in exceptional cases, emphasizing the trial court's prerogative to award a sentence under Section 306 IPC.

quotes.text: We must also emphasize that the interference of the appellate court on the quantum of sentence should be rare and only in exceptional cases. Section 306 of the IPC provides for a sentence which may extend to 10 years.

sentencing_rationale.value: The final sentence was imposed based on the trial court's finding that the incident was a spontaneous family quarrel and there was no misbehaviour on the part of the accused over a period of time.

quotes.text: The trial court had given a positive finding that there was no misbehaviour on the part of the appellant over a period of time and the incident was a spontaneous one arising out of a family quarrel in the morning.

other_sentence_order.value: The Supreme Court quashed the High Court's enhanced sentence and confirmed the trial court's judgment. It also directed the release of the appellant if not required in any other case.

quotes.text: We accordingly allow the appeal, quash the sentence awarded by the High Court and confirm the judgment of the Trial Court. In the meantime, we also direct that the appellant who is in custody, shall be released forthwith if not required in connection with any other case.
